publication: Draft follow-up only. User approved PR72/73; this new change awaits review.
purpose: Exclude empty noindex listing pages from multilingual alternate relationships and guard the generated SEO graph.

initialAudit.issue: All twelve links targeted existing noindex post listings with no articles.

scope.fix: Post/digest alternates include only languages with actual entries; empty listings emit no hreflang.
scope.guard: Build validates generated self-canonical/indexable targets, matching language, unique absolute links, self reference, reciprocal links, existing English x-default policy and sitemap/HTML alternate agreement.

review.type: Self AI review; not independent or human review

findings.issue: An empty translated post index is a real URL but noindex, so route existence alone is insufficient.
findings.resolution: Filter using published entries and verify final emitted metadata.

findings.issue: Sitemap does not repeat hreflang for every static page; Google accepts HTML or XML annotation.
findings.resolution: Compare annotations where XML provides them; do not require duplicate implementation for every URL.

findings.issue: Noindex search pages and old redirect shells are intentionally not alternate destinations.
findings.resolution: Exclude them from eligible targets, retain normal navigation and existing redirects.

findings.issue: Passing static checks is not evidence of Google indexing or higher rank.
findings.resolution: State the static scope in CLI output, README and PR.

validation.mutationTests: Eight test methods cover noindex/none, refresh, wrong canonical, absent/nonreciprocal targets, wrong/duplicate/missing locale, relative/external/query/fragment URL, x-default policy, XML/HTML disagreement, duplicate/empty sitemap and bad namespace.
validation.generatedHTMLTest: All eight post listings; en/ko reciprocal links retained, six empty lists remain noindex without hreflang or sitemap loc.

limits: No actual search-engine index or rank claim.
No new translations or article rewrites.
Reciprocal metadata does not certify semantic translation equivalence.
External alternate URLs are prohibited by this site-specific guard, not by a universal hreflang rule.
